newsitem.title: GERMANY: Survey - 37 pct see Kohl team back after '98 poll.
newsitem.headline: Survey - 37 pct see Kohl team back after '98 poll.

text.p: A survey of prominent figures in German politics, media and industry found 37 percent of respondents expect Chancellor Helmut Kohl's coalition to survive in its present form after 1998 elections.

The results of the survey of 278 people were published on Tuesday. The ruling coalition comprises Kohl's Christian Democrats (CDU), Bavarian sister party the Christian Social Union (CSU) and liberal Free Democrats (FDP).

The survey, conducted by German public relations agency Kohtes und Klewes and the Emnid research institute, showed that 34 percent expected a new "red-green" coalition of Social Democrats (SPD) and environmentalist Greens.
Only 17 foresaw a grand coalition between Kohl's CDU/CSU and the second largest party in parliament, the SPD.
The survey was conducted in April among 61 parliamentary deputies, 86 top government officials, 78 senior editors and 53 leading representatives from industry and associations.
It was published by Reuters and German business magazine Wirtschaftswoche and is carried out three times a year.

When asked which candidate for chancellor would best help their party win next year's election, 80 percent named Kohl as the CDU's number one candidate, while they picked Lower Saxony state premier Gerhard Schoeder for the SPD.

Only 14 percent thought current SPD leader Oskar Lafontaine would maximise his party's chances of election victory, while 17 percent said CDU/CSU parliamentary leader Wolfgang Schaeuble would do better than Kohl as chancellor candidate.
